title: Gallery fire event still

title: Gallery AI tracking at normal speed
description: A stationary brown tank tracks a moving player across the existing deterministic gallery moment at normal simulation speed. This is generic tracking evidence, not evidence of turret shimmer or a deadband choice.
altText: A stationary brown tank rotates its turret to follow a blue tank driving laterally across the felt arena.

title: Gallery ricochet still
description: The deterministic ricochet moment at the tick the shell leaves the wall. A second still recipe on a different scenario, so the still path is not exercised by gallery.fire.still alone -- and one whose captured tick is not the tick of its first expected event, which the fire recipe cannot show.
altText: A blue tank on the felt arena floor, its shell against the dark angled wall it is bouncing off.

title: Gallery drive at normal speed
description: A tank driving across the arena at normal simulation speed. A second temporal recipe on a different scenario, so the clip path is not exercised by gallery.ai-tracking.normal alone; the motion here is a translating hull rather than a rotating turret.
altText: A blue tank driving across the felt arena floor, laying a tread trail.

title: Gallery AI last-seen memory at normal speed
description: A stationary brown tank loses sight of the player behind a wall, holds its turret on the last position it actually observed for AI_LAST_SEEN_TICKS, then hands off to the idle search sweep. Issue #372's artefact. Shot from the TOP view, not the game camera: the whole content of the clip is where a turret points relative to a target it cannot see, and the game camera's oblique angle foreshortens exactly that bearing. The clip is evidence for a judgement -- whether this reads as attentive rather than omniscient -- not a measurement; the measurable parts are pinned in src/render/gallery/moments.test.ts.
altText: Top-down view: a brown tank's turret follows a blue tank until the blue tank passes behind a grey wall, then stays pointed at the spot where it disappeared while the blue tank drives back and forth elsewhere, and finally begins sweeping.

title: Campaign level 1 at normal speed, pp1Roles off
description: The baseline half of issue #720's matched pair: campaign level 1, seed 1, the scripted player, shipped role budgets. The whole round of the real application at wall-clock pace, from the end of the round-start countdown to the last frame before the outcome panel (under a 60 s ceiling), recorded from the compositor and resampled to 30 fps. The page runs its production game loop; nothing steps the simulation. Needs a build that names its commit (VITE_BUILD_SHA) and a host GPU for the delivered-rate gate.

title: Campaign combat at normal speed, in a documentation profile
description: Campaign level 4, seed 1, the scripted player, shipped behaviour and no experimental flags: the full enemy roster fighting at wall-clock pace, recorded from the compositor. A DOCUMENTATION profile rather than a review profile -- 640x400, an 8 s window and 15 fps, so the GIF preview fits a repository page instead of the 1280x800/60 s/30 fps that `flow.campaign-round.pp1roles-off` uses for frame-accurate review. The MP4 remains the timing-faithful artifact; the GIF is a preview. A flow evaluates no simulation events, so this recipe cannot assert that a shot or a hit falls inside the window -- that is what the editorial review is for. Needs a build that names its commit (VITE_BUILD_SHA) and a host GPU for the delivered-rate gate: the gate is the same 45 every flow recipe uses, and neither a SwiftShader host nor the hosted capture runner can hold it, so publication footage is generated on a workstation.
altText: Animation of a Tanks! campaign round in play, the player's tank fighting several enemy tanks across a walled arena.

title: A four-player versus round at normal speed, in a documentation profile
description: A free-for-all versus session with four tanks sharing the board, level 1, seed 1, shipped behaviour and no experimental flags. The same documentation profile as `flow.campaign-round.docs`: 640x400, an 8 s window, 15 fps, MP4 plus a GIF preview. The versus-round flow waits for the stock strip before it records, so a session that silently ran campaign-shaped fails rather than publishing the wrong mode. A flow evaluates no simulation events, so this recipe cannot assert the bots engage each other inside the window; the editorial review is what confirms it. Needs a build that names its commit (VITE_BUILD_SHA) and a host GPU for the delivered-rate gate: the gate is the same 45 every flow recipe uses, and neither a SwiftShader host nor the hosted capture runner can hold it, so publication footage is generated on a workstation.
altText: Animation of a Tanks! local versus round, four differently coloured tanks fighting on one arena with a stock counter along the top.
